Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: E-Houwiya provides full digital authentication functionality: two-factor authentication (login/password + SMS OTP), X.509 PKI certificates and cryptographic keys, qualified digital signatures legally equivalent to handwritten signatures, and single sign-on (SSO) access to government portals. The 2024 biometric CIN law also includes an authentication certificate on the chip (Article 2 of Organic Law 2024-22).
revision_notes: Sources fetched and confirmed: idtechwire.com (19 Mar 2025) describes E-Houwiya's two-factor authentication, X.509 certificates and qualified digital signature; legislation-securite.tn confirms Organic Law 2024-22 (11 Mar 2024) provides for an electronic authentication certificate on the biometric CIN chip. Evidence fully supports Value Code 2 (Yes). Score confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Tunisia's E-Houwiya national digital identity system provides full digital authentication functionality, combining two-factor login (identifier plus SMS one-time password), personal X.509 PKI certificates and cryptographic signing keys, and a qualified digital signature that is legally equivalent to a handwritten signature. Authentication is also embedded in the biometric national identity card framework introduced by Organic Law 2024-22, which provides for an authentication certificate on the card's chip.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: E-Houwiya serves as the centralized SSO for Tunisian government portals including E-Bawaba (official e-government portal), E-CNAM (national health insurance), E-People, E-CNSS (social security), Madrassati (education), and E-Barid (official government email). Citizens can access thousands of online administrative services using E-Houwiya authentication.
revision_notes: Confirmed via idtechwire.com and mobileidworld.com (19-20 Mar 2025), and Access Now (Feb 2023), which independently describe E-Houwiya's SSO role across e-Bawaba, e-CNAM, e-People, e-CNSS and e-Barid. Evidence supports Value Code 2 (Yes). Score confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: E-Houwiya operates as Tunisia's centralised single sign-on mechanism for government digital services, giving citizens authenticated access to portals including e-Bawaba (the official e-government portal), e-CNAM (national health insurance), e-People, e-CNSS (social security), Madrassati (education) and e-Barid (government email). While not yet legally mandatory for most services, adoption is growing and it now also underpins onboarding to digital banking and fintech services.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Judicial oversight of the ID system is indirect. INPDP decisions can be appealed to the Tunis Court of Appeal and further to the Court of Cassation (per Organic Law 2004-63). There is no ID-specific judicial oversight mechanism; courts provide general oversight through the appeals process. The 2024 Biometric ID law requires INPDP consultation for implementing decrees. No dedicated ID tribunal or specialized judicial body exists.
revision_notes: Confirmed via DLA Piper Data Protection Laws of the World, Tunisia authority page (last modified 12 Feb 2026): 'The decisions of the Instance can be appealed before the Court of Appeal of Tunis and before the Court of Cassation.' This directly corroborates the original comment. Value Code 2 ('Yes, but not specific to ID') confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Judicial oversight of Tunisia's ID and data protection framework is indirect and general rather than ID-specific. Decisions of the Instance Nationale de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (INPDP) - the body regulating ID-related personal data - can be appealed before the Court of Appeal of Tunis and, subsequently, before the Court of Cassation. No dedicated ID tribunal or ID-specific judicial mechanism exists.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Civil registration (Madania system) is partially integrated with the national ID system. The RIUC was initialized from Madania + CIN data and permanent links for real-time birth/death updates were planned. CIN enrollment requires a birth extract from Madania. The World Bank diagnostic notes the RIUC system links CR and CIN but full real-time interoperability has not been completed. IS social identifier queries Madania via 8 attributes. Full integration is underway but not yet complete.
revision_notes: World Bank ID4D diagnostic and CRVS Centre of Excellence report confirm the RIUC design draws on Madania and CIN data; a February 2024 Cybernetica announcement confirms the TunXRoad interoperability platform (successor project) remains under active development with former minister Nizar Ben Neji, indicating integration is ongoing but still incomplete as of 2024. Value Code 2 (Partial integration) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Tunisia's civil registration system (Madania) and identity infrastructure are partially integrated through the Registre de l'Identifiant Unique du Citoyen (RIUC), established by Decree-Law 2020-17, which draws on both civil registration and CIN data to assign each citizen a unique lifelong identifier. A national interoperability platform, TunXRoad (built on the X-Road/UXP technology supplied by Estonia's Cybernetica under a 2024 cooperation agreement), is being developed to link the civil register with sectoral systems, but full real-time interoperability between civil registration and the ID ecosystem has not yet been completed.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Organic Law No. 2004-63 (July 27, 2004) on the Protection of Personal Data is in force. It establishes data subject rights (access, rectification, opposition), requires prior declaration/authorization for processing, mandates consent, and includes criminal sanctions. Critics note it is outdated and a new GDPR-aligned law has been drafted since 2018 but not yet enacted as of 2025.
revision_notes: Confirmed via legislation-securite.tn (full text of Organic Law 2004-63) and DLA Piper Data Protection Laws of the World, Tunisia page (updated 12 Feb 2026), which confirms the 2004 law remains in force and that a GDPR-aligned draft from 2018 has still not passed. Value Code 2 (Yes) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Tunisia has comprehensive data protection legislation, Organic Law No. 2004-63 of 27 July 2004, on the Protection of Personal Data, which grants data subjects rights of access, rectification and objection, requires prior declaration or authorisation for processing, and includes criminal sanctions for breaches. It applies to personal data linked to the ID system. A GDPR-aligned replacement law has been drafted since 2018 but had not been enacted as of early 2026.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Instance Nationale de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (INPDP) was established by Decree No. 2007-3003 under Organic Law 2004-63. It oversees data processing registrations/authorizations, handles complaints, issues decisions, and its decisions can be appealed to the Tunis Court of Appeal. INPDP must be consulted on legislation affecting personal data (though this was bypassed for E-Houwiya and the subsidy platform, raising civil society concerns).
revision_notes: Confirmed via INPDP's own website (inpdp.tn) and DLA Piper's Tunisia authority page (current as of Feb 2026), both describing INPDP's statutory powers and continued operation. Access Now (2023) corroborates the concern that INPDP consultation has occasionally been bypassed (e.g. for Decree-Law 54 and E-Houwiya), consistent with the original comment. Value Code 2 (Yes) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: The Instance Nationale de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (INPDP), established under Decree No. 2007-3003 pursuant to Organic Law 2004-63, is Tunisia's data protection authority. It authorises and registers data processing declarations, handles complaints, issues legally appealable decisions, and holds a formal (though sometimes bypassed) consultative role on legislation affecting personal data. It is the oldest data protection authority in Africa and the Arab world.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: All core ID systems are maintained by Tunisian government entities: Madania CR system by Ministry of Local Affairs (MALE) via the National Informatics Center (CNI); CIN system by Ministry of Interior (Technical Police); E-Houwiya by Ministry of Communication Technologies and its affiliated entities (National Digital Certification Agency, CNI, local telecom operators); RIUC under MALE/MTCEN. E-Houwiya was developed with Estonian eGA advisory support (MOU 2022) but operated domestically.
revision_notes: Confirmed via idtechwire.com/biometricupdate.com (2025), which describe E-Houwiya's domestic operating entities and the advisory (not operational) role of Estonian partners, and the World Bank diagnostic which confirms Madania/CIN are run by domestic ministries. Value Code 3 (All in-country) confirmed unchanged, noting the advisory/technology-partnership role of Estonian and Cybernetica support does not amount to foreign vendor control of day-to-day operations.
revised_comments: Tunisia's foundational and digital ID systems are managed and maintained by domestic public institutions: the Madania civil registration system by the Ministry of Local Affairs via the National Informatics Centre (CNI); the CIN by the Ministry of Interior; and E-Houwiya by the Ministry of Communication Technologies together with the National Digital Certification Agency, CNI and local telecom operators. Estonia's e-Governance Academy provided technical advisory support under a 2022 memorandum of understanding, and Cybernetica supplied interoperability platform technology in 2024, but day-to-day operation and credential production remain in-country.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: Tunisia's ID systems are primarily domestically financed. The CIN system is funded through the Ministry of Interior budget; the Madania civil registration system is funded via local government and MALE. The E-Houwiya system is operated by the Ministry of Communication Technologies and affiliated state entities (CNI, National Digital Certification Agency, telecom operators). The World Bank provided a diagnostic (2020) and advisory support, and Estonian eGA provided technical advisory (MOU 2022), but operational funding is domestic.
revision_notes: Confirmed via idtechwire.com/biometricupdate.com (2025) and the World Bank diagnostic, which describe domestic ministry budget lines for CIN, Madania and E-Houwiya, with international partners limited to advisory/diagnostic roles rather than ongoing operational financing. Value Code 3 (Primarily domestic funding) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Tunisia's ID systems are funded primarily through domestic public budgets: the CIN through the Ministry of Interior, Madania through local government and the Ministry of Local Affairs, and E-Houwiya through the Ministry of Communication Technologies and its affiliated state entities. The World Bank has provided technical diagnostics and advisory support and Estonia's e-Governance Academy has provided advisory assistance, but core operational funding is domestic.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: All major ID databases are fully digital. The Madania civil registration system (SQL Server, fully operational since April 2005) centralizes all civil registration across 350 municipalities. The CIN database is fully electronic (Cobol/VSE-CICS system). The RIUC holds 15 million records in a centralized Oracle database. Social protection IS database uses Oracle 12c. Paper registers are also maintained for legal validity of civil status but all administration is digital.
revision_notes: Confirmed via the World Bank ID4D diagnostic and the CRVS Centre of Excellence Tunisia case study, both describing Madania, CIN and RIUC as electronic databases. Value Code 3 (Digital) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Tunisia's core identity databases are fully digital. The Madania civil registration system, running on SQL Server and operational nationwide since April 2005, centralises civil registration data from all 350 municipalities. The CIN database is maintained electronically by the Ministry of Interior, and the RIUC holds around 15 million records in a centralised Oracle database. Paper civil status registers are retained in parallel for legal purposes, but administration of the records is digital.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Tunisia operates two foundational digital ID systems fully deployed nationwide: the CIN (Carte d'Identité Nationale, paper card with digital database, mandatory for citizens 18+) and the E-Houwiya mobile digital identity launched August 2022 covering all Tunisian citizens. A biometric CIN was legislated (Organic Law 2024-22) and rollout was planned for H1 2025. The existing systems are digitally managed and nationally deployed.
revision_notes: Confirmed via idtechwire.com (2025), Access Now (Mar 2024, confirming passage of the Biometric ID and Passport laws), and legislation-securite.tn (Organic Law 2024-22 text). A February 2026 update (African Manager) notes the biometric CIN and passport rollout remains 'at an advanced stage, despite some delays', indicating the biometric upgrade is not yet fully complete, but the existing CIN and E-Houwiya systems are both operational nationwide. Value Code 5 (Fully deployed nationwide) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Tunisia operates fully deployed, nationwide foundational and digital identity systems. The Carte d'Identité Nationale (CIN), mandatory for citizens from age 15 (lowered from 18 by Organic Law 2024-22 of March 2024), has been issued for decades and is now being progressively upgraded to a biometric, chip-based credential. E-Houwiya, a state-recognised mobile digital identity legally equivalent to face-to-face identification, has been operational nationwide since August 2022 and continues to expand its use cases, including banking sector onboarding since early 2025.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: Tunisia's E-Houwiya functions as SSO across multiple government portals (E-Bawaba, E-CNAM, E-People, E-CNSS, Madrassati). The RIUC (Registre de l'Identifiant Unique du Citoyen) was being implemented as a central dictionary linking sectoral identifiers across agencies via TunXRoad platform. However, the World Bank diagnostic noted low integration and interoperability between systems in 2020, partially improved with IS social identifier linking social protection funds.
revision_notes: Confirmed via idtechwire.com/mobileidworld.com (2025) for SSO functionality, and a February 2024 Cybernetica announcement confirming the TunXRoad interoperability platform is under active development. Value Code 2 (Yes) confirmed unchanged, noting interoperability remains partial in practice.
revised_comments: Tunisia's digital ID architecture is designed for interoperability. E-Houwiya functions as a single sign-on layer across multiple government portals (e-Bawaba, e-CNAM, e-People, e-CNSS, Madrassati), and the Registre de l'Identifiant Unique du Citoyen (RIUC) is intended to act as a central identity dictionary linking sectoral identifiers. A national interoperability platform (TunXRoad, built on Cybernetica's X-Road/UXP technology under a 2024 government-to-government agreement) is under active development to formalise data exchange between agencies, though sectoral integration has historically been limited.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: The CIN is required for healthcare access in Tunisia. Free care cards and reduced-price healthcare cards require CIN copies from all family members over 18. The CNAM (national health insurance) digital card distribution began in 2019. Access to public health establishments and CNAM services requires identity verification via CIN. E-Houwiya serves as SSO for E-CNAM portal. The CIN is mandatory for healthcare access.
revision_notes: Original source (social.gov.tn 'attributing-free-health-care-cards' page) returned an HTTP 403 error and could not be verified directly; confirmed instead via the Ministry of Social Affairs' French-language equivalent page (social.gov.tn/fr/attribution-de-cartes-de-soins-gratuites) and CNAM's own FAQ page, both of which state a copy of the CIN is required, plus the World Bank ID4D diagnostic. Value Code 3 (Mandatory) confirmed unchanged; recommend the dead English-language URL be replaced in the master dataset.
revised_comments: The national identity card (CIN) is required to access subsidised and free public healthcare in Tunisia. Applications for the free healthcare card (carte de soins gratuits) and reduced-cost care require a copy of the national identity card for each family member aged 18 or over, per the Ministry of Social Affairs' eligibility procedures, and registration with the national health insurance fund (CNAM) similarly requires the CIN. E-Houwiya also provides single sign-on access to the e-CNAM online health insurance portal.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Non-Tunisian residents are required to carry a residence card (carte de résidence) issued by the Ministry of Interior, usable for KYC purposes. The CIN is for Tunisian nationals only. The E-Houwiya digital ID is explicitly limited to Tunisian nationals (aged 18+ holding a CIN). The RIUC system covers Tunisian nationals only. Non-nationals have some access to an identity credential (residence card) but not the national digital ID system.
revision_notes: Confirmed via the E-Houwiya App Store listing, which explicitly limits eligibility to Tunisians residing in Tunisia and abroad holding a CIN, and Smile ID's country overview, which describes the resident card as the relevant KYC document for non-nationals. Value Code 2 (Some) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Non-Tunisian residents, including refugees and permanent residents, are not eligible for the CIN or for E-Houwiya, both of which are restricted to Tunisian nationals aged 18 or over holding a national identity card. Non-nationals instead carry a residence card (carte de résidence) issued by the Ministry of Interior, which can serve as an identity and KYC document. Eligibility for the core digital ID ecosystem is therefore limited to a subset of the resident population.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: Civil registration (Madania) covers 99% of the population. The CIN covers approximately 90% of adults aged 18+ (World Bank estimate). The RIUC holds records for 15 million individuals. E-Houwiya had 200,000 subscribers as of March 2025 (lower digital ID coverage). The foundational ID coverage (civil register + CIN combined) exceeds 89% of the total population.
revision_notes: HUMAN REVIEW FLAGGED: the variable is ambiguous as to whether 'digital ID credentials' refers to Tunisia's foundational ID system (civil register + CIN, providing the ~90% coverage figure the original score of 5/>89% rests on) or specifically to the electronic/mobile credential E-Houwiya (only c. 200,000 subscribers as of Mar 2025, i.e. under 3% of the eligible adult population, which would score 1/<20%). The World Bank diagnostic also states the pre-2024 CIN itself 'is not electronic' and authentication involves only a manual check, undermining its classification as a 'digital ID credential'; it also notes CIN coverage estimates range 84-90% and are 'pending inputs from the Ministry of Interior', i.e. imprecise. Sources checked: World Bank ID4D Tunisia diagnostic (2020, CIN coverage) and idtechwire.com/mobileidworld.com (Mar 2025, E-Houwiya subscriber count). For consistency with the 'Digital ID System Exists' row, which treats CIN and E-Houwiya jointly as the national digital ID system, the original Value Code 5 has not been changed, but the discrepancy between foundational and strictly-digital coverage is material and should be resolved by a human reviewer, ideally by clarifying the intended scope of 'digital ID' for this indicator across the whole dataset.
revised_comments: Foundational identity coverage in Tunisia is high: civil registration (Madania) covers an estimated 99% of the population, and the national identity card (CIN) covers an estimated 84-90% of adults aged 18 and over, per World Bank estimates. Uptake of the specifically electronic/mobile credential, E-Houwiya, remains far lower, with around 200,000 subscribers (including Tunisians abroad) as of March 2025, against an adult population of several million.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: Decree-Law 2023-17 on cybersecurity mandates annual IT security audits for entities processing personal data, with reporting to the National Cybersecurity Agency (ANCS). The Ministry of Communication Technologies issued decisions on procedures for granting a 'secure' label to software/equipment (September 2023). Mandatory periodic security audits of information systems are required. However, civil society notes that transparency of security reviews for E-Houwiya is limited.
revision_notes: Confirmed via DLA Piper's Tunisia data protection page (current as of Feb 2026), which describes Decree-Law 2023-17 and its September 2023 implementing orders in detail, and the Paradigm Initiative LONDA 2023 report, which raises transparency concerns specific to E-Houwiya. Value Code 2 (Yes) confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Tunisia has a statutory requirement for regular security reviews of systems processing personal data. Decree-Law No. 2023-17 of 11 March 2023 on cybersecurity mandates periodic technical audits for organisations subject to its scope, with results reported to the National Cybersecurity Agency (ANCS), and implementing ministerial orders from September 2023 set out audit classification criteria and a 'secure' labelling scheme. Civil society organisations note that transparency around security reviews specific to E-Houwiya remains limited.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: The CIN is mandatory for access to social services in Tunisia. The Ministry of Social Affairs requires CIN copies from all family members over 18 for eligibility assessment for social programs (Amen social program, free healthcare cards). The World Bank diagnostic confirms all functional ID systems require CIN as proof of identity for transactions such as collecting social security payments. No administrative procedure can be completed without presenting the CIN.
revision_notes: Original source (social.gov.tn 'attributing-free-health-care-cards' page) returned an HTTP 403 error; confirmed instead via the Ministry of Social Affairs' French-language equivalent page and the CRVS Centre of Excellence Tunisia case study, which both describe the CIN requirement for Amen Social enrolment, plus the World Bank ID4D diagnostic. Value Code 3 (Mandatory) confirmed unchanged; recommend the dead English-language URL be replaced in the master dataset.
revised_comments: The national identity card is mandatory for accessing social assistance in Tunisia. Enrolment in the Amen Social programme and applications for free or reduced-cost healthcare cards both require a copy of the national identity card for every family member aged 18 or over, alongside a birth certificate. The World Bank's ID4D diagnostic confirms that no social protection transaction, including collection of social security payments, can be completed without presenting the CIN.
